Firm rule stands: treat >~6-8% above-EMA extension as size-DOWN or wait-for-pullback; when it co-occurs with a shallow cross, SKIP. STACKED-FLAG entries (shallow cross + extended above EMA + thin liquidity together) -- SKIP, not size-down: PDBC (0.15% cross + ~6% ext + thin liq, Jul 24) stopped -2.40%. One flag -> size down; two or more stacked -> skip. Applied correctly repeatedly: SLV skipped Aug 28 (two flags), MSTR skipped Sep 1 (three flags), EWZ skipped Sep 2 (0.033% noise cross + 7.05% ext). HAL 9/4 was a legitimate size-down (two SOFT flags: 0.298% cross + 657k borderline liq, NOT extended at 5.69%) -- the boundary case, still -0.58% and worth watching.
